title: Ephemeral Wonders
subtitle: Light, cosmos, ancient echoes & living marvels

clues.clue: This arc of colors appears when sunlight is refracted and reflected inside falling raindrops.
clues.fact: No two people see quite the same rainbow; each eye catches light from different drops.

clues.clue: In a vacuum, light covers roughly 300,000 of these units every single second.
clues.fact: Sunlight needs about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.

clues.clue: Light with wavelengths just shorter than violet, invisible to us, causes sunburn.
clues.fact: Bees and many birds can see ultraviolet patterns hidden from human eyes.

clues.clue: Named for a British physicist, this scattering of sunlight by air molecules makes the sky blue.
clues.fact: Short blue wavelengths scatter far more strongly in air than long red ones.

clues.clue: This English polymath's double-slit experiment in the early 1800s showed light behaves as a wave.
clues.fact: Bright and dark bands revealed light waves adding together and cancelling out.

clues.clue: The star at the center of our solar system, it is also the closest star to Earth.
clues.fact: The Sun holds about 99.8% of all the mass in our solar system.

clues.clue: The largest planet in our solar system, it hosts a giant storm called the Great Red Spot.
clues.fact: The Great Red Spot is a storm wider than the entire Earth.

clues.clue: About 2.5 million light-years away, this is the Milky Way's nearest large spiral galaxy.
clues.fact: On a dark night, Andromeda glows to the naked eye as a faint, ancient smudge.

clues.clue: First reported in 1965, this faint afterglow of the Big Bang fills the whole sky with microwaves.
clues.answer: What is the cosmic microwave background?
clues.fact: Its discoverers first suspected pigeons nesting in their antenna of causing the hiss.

clues.clue: These spinning neutron stars, some rotating hundreds of times a second, sweep radio beams like lighthouses.
clues.fact: Jocelyn Bell Burnell spotted the first pulsar's steady ticking in 1967.

clues.clue: Near Cairo, it is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.
clues.answer: What is the Great Pyramid of Giza?
clues.fact: It was the tallest human-made structure on Earth for nearly 3,800 years.

clues.clue: This prehistoric stone circle on England's Salisbury Plain aligns with the summer solstice sunrise.
clues.fact: Its smaller bluestones were hauled from Wales's Preseli Hills, about 140 miles away.

clues.clue: Found in 1799 and carved with the same decree in three scripts, it unlocked Egyptian hieroglyphs.
clues.fact: Jean-Francois Champollion announced his decipherment in 1822.

clues.clue: Hiram Bingham brought this Inca citadel high in Peru's Andes to world attention in 1911.
clues.fact: Its mortarless stones fit so tightly that a knife blade cannot slip between them.

clues.clue: Recovered from a Greek shipwreck in 1901, this bronze-geared device modeled the cycles of the heavens.
clues.fact: Often called the first analog computer, it predicted eclipses over 2,000 years ago.

clues.clue: Earth's largest living animal, this ocean giant can reach about 30 meters in length.
clues.fact: Its low, haunting calls can travel hundreds of kilometers through the sea.

clues.clue: This process lets plants turn sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into sugar and oxygen.
clues.fact: Ocean phytoplankton produce roughly half of the oxygen made on Earth.

clues.clue: The world's largest coral reef system, it stretches along the coast of Queensland, Australia.
clues.answer: What is the Great Barrier Reef?
clues.fact: Built from nearly 3,000 individual reefs, it can be seen from orbit.

clues.clue: Nicknamed the water bear, this microscopic animal can survive the vacuum of open space.
clues.fact: In 2007, tardigrades survived 10 days exposed to open space aboard a Russian satellite.

clues.clue: These single-celled plankton make breaking waves sparkle electric blue on some nights.
clues.fact: They flash when disturbed, likely to startle the creatures that would eat them.

clues.clue: Sound cannot travel through this empty region with no air, which is why space is silent.
clues.fact: Sound moves about four times faster through water than through air.

clues.clue: This unit of frequency, named for a German physicist, equals one cycle per second.
clues.fact: Human hearing spans roughly 20 to 20,000 hertz.

clues.clue: This ancient timekeeper tells the hour by the shadow its gnomon casts across a marked face.
clues.fact: Egyptian shadow clocks were tracking the hours more than 3,000 years ago.

clues.clue: In October 1947, Chuck Yeager's Bell X-1 became the first plane to officially break this in level flight.
clues.fact: Yeager named his X-1 'Glamorous Glennis' after his wife.

clues.clue: Atomic clocks define the second using about 9.19 billion oscillations tied to atoms of this element.
clues.fact: One SI second is exactly 9,192,631,770 cycles of cesium-133 radiation.

final_jeopardy.clue: Named for the Greek word for the Sun, this element was spotted in sunlight's spectrum in 1868 before it was found on Earth.
final_jeopardy.fact: William Ramsay finally isolated helium on Earth in 1895.
